what: Part A: the published Z+jets reference, CMS-SMP-19-009

labels.exclusive_sigma_pb: VERIFIED BY RUNNING (downloaded from HEPData Table 1a and parsed)
labels.inclusive_sigma_pb: DERIVED by summing the exclusive bins; the measurement stops at 8 jets and the uncertainty is a quadrature sum that ignores bin-to-bin correlation
labels.prediction_over_data: UNVERIFIED -- read off Fig. 4a of the publication by eye, because this HEPData record tabulates the measurement but not the predictions. Reading uncertainty about +-0.02, which is NOT the theory uncertainty
labels.definitions: VERBATIM QUOTES from the arXiv source of arXiv:2205.02872

jets.quote: Jets are formed from the particles reconstructed by the PF algorithm using the FastJet software package, and the anti-kT jet clustering algorithm with a distance parameter R of 0.4. ... Tight identification quality criteria, based on the fraction of energy carried by charged and neutral hadrons, are applied to jets ... Jets are required to have |eta| < 2.4, to be separated from all selected lepton candidates by at least a distance Delta R = 0.4, and have a pT larger than 30 GeV for the single-differential cross sections and 20 GeV for the double-differential ones.
jets.algorithm: anti-kT, R = 0.4, PF + charged hadron subtraction
jets.b_tag_note: the paper applies no b-tag requirement or veto anywhere in the jet-multiplicity definition, so b jets are counted as jets

leptons.quote: After offline reconstruction, two leptons are required with the first having pT > 30 GeV and the second having pT > 20 GeV. We require that the two electrons (muons) with highest pT form a pair of oppositely charged leptons with an invariant mass in the range (91 +- 20 GeV). ... For both electrons and muons, medium identification criteria are applied.
leptons.eta_quote: Electron candidates within the geometrical acceptance of |eta| < 2.4, excluding the barrel-to-endcap (1.444 < |eta| < 1.566) transition regions of the ECAL ... Muon candidates within the geometrical acceptance of |eta| < 2.4

particle_level.quote: The particle-level objects are defined with a lifetime of c*tau > 1 cm (excluding neutrinos) and identified using the same algorithms as used for the data. Leptons are stable particles coming from Z boson decays, dressed by adding the momenta of all photons within R < 0.1 of their directions.

trigger.quote: Candidate events are selected online using single-lepton triggers that require at least one isolated electron (muon) with pT > 25 (24) GeV and |eta| < 2.4.

normalisation.quote: the simulated samples are normalized to the integrated luminosity of the data sample using their respective cross sections.

MG5_aMC NLO FxFx (<=2j NLO + PS).quote: For the simulation of the signal, we use a sample generated at next-to-leading order (NLO) with MG5_aMC versions 2.2.2 and 2.3.2 using the FxFx merging scheme. Parton showering and hadronization are simulated with PYTHIA8 (version 8.212) using the CUETP8M1 tune. The matrix element includes Z boson production with up to two additional jets generated at NLO with MG5_aMC, effectively yielding leading order (LO) accuracy for Z+3 jets.

MG5_aMC LO MLM (<=4j LO + PS).quote: For the LO MG5_aMC, the generator calculates LO matrix elements (MEs) for five processes: pp -> Z + N_jets with N = 0, ..., 4. The NNPDF 3.0 LO PDF is used and alpha_s(mZ) is set to 0.130. ... The ME and parton shower matching is done using the kT-MLM scheme with the matching scale set at 19 GeV for the LO MG5_aMC.

differences_from_our_setup.theirs: legacy 2016 ReReco (the 2016 analysis campaign of CMS-SMP-19-009)
differences_from_our_setup.matters: different jet energy corrections, different pileup treatment and a different jet ID training; the two are not the same detector calibration
G+H is the post-VFP part of 2016; the pileup profile and the tracker condition differ from the 2016 average

differences_from_our_setup.theirs: particle level, unfolded for detector effects
differences_from_our_setup.matters: their data/prediction ratio has the detector taken out of it; ours has it still in. Any difference between the two ratios is therefore a detector-level statement about our setup
we can tighten the leading lepton to 30 but cannot lower the subleading one to 20 without replacing the delivered lepton selection, which this study may not do
we count slightly more forward jets; this is closed in the paper-like definition

differences_from_our_setup.ours: excluded from the light-jet count the excess was seen in
differences_from_our_setup.matters: closed in the paper-like definition, and measured separately in Part B1

differences_from_our_setup.theirs: MG5_aMC FxFx <=2j NLO, CUETP8M1 tune, NNPDF3.0
differences_from_our_setup.matters: the SAME generator and merging scheme at the same matrix-element multiplicity, with a newer tune (CP5 rather than CUETP8M1) and a UL campaign. The published prediction is therefore directly informative about ours

differences_from_our_setup.theirs: a full background estimate including ttbar, single top, dibosons and a data-driven nonresonant background
differences_from_our_setup.matters: single top and dibosons are missing from our simulation; they matter most at high jet multiplicity
